title: Fermionic Hamiltonian engineering with local control
authors: Özgün Kum, Matthias Zipper, Ludwig Mathey, Martin Kliesch
abstract: Quantum simulators enable the exploration of complex quantum phenomena in condensed-matter systems by reproducing their dynamics on controllable quantum devices. However, experimental constraints often restrict the class of Hamiltonians that can be realized natively. Hamiltonian engineering addresses this limitation by expanding the set of accessible target Hamiltonians from a fixed system Hamiltonian defined by the hardware. We introduce a new framework for fermionic Hamiltonian engineering based on conjugating free evolution under the system Hamiltonian with sequences of experimentally feasible local fermionic unitaries. The required sequences and free-evolution times are obtained efficiently via a linear program. By interleaving system evolution with these local unitaries, our method realizes effective time evolution under a broad class of target Hamiltonians, with intrinsic robustness to finite-pulse-time errors. In particular, we demonstrate that arbitrary complex tunnelling coefficients can be realized, constrained only by the connectivity of the underlying system Hamiltonian. We illustrate this capability by engineering the dynamics of the non-interacting Harper-Hofstadter model on a 1088-mode lattice and an interacting Fermi-Hubbard chain with complex tunnelling coefficients. By construction, our approach avoids the continuous energy absorption inherent to Floquet engineering.
summary: The paper presents a novel framework for fermionic Hamiltonian engineering that allows researchers to simulate target Hamiltonians unattainable with the underlying quantum hardware. By interleaving free evolution under the system Hamiltonian with local unitary pulses, it achieves robust control over complex couplings, notably realizing arbitrary complex tunneling coefficients.
main_problem: The primary goal is to engineer effective time evolution under a desired target fermionic Hamiltonian ($H_T$) that may not be natively supported by the quantum hardware.
main_result: The framework successfully realizes arbitrary complex tunneling coefficients and simulates dynamics robustly, avoiding energy absorption issues associated with standard Floquet engineering techniques.
method: It achieves this by conjugating free evolution under the native system Hamiltonian ($H_S$) with sequences of experimentally feasible local fermionic unitaries, optimized via a linear program.
model_or_system: The method is applied to general fermionic quantum many-body systems, exemplified by the non-interacting Harper-Hofstadter model and interacting Fermi-Hubbard chains. The underlying physics relates to ultracold atoms in optical lattices.
key_observables: State fidelity ($F$), energy expectation value ($\langle H_S angle$), and bond currents ($\langle J_{kj} angle$).
important_parameters: The ratio of interaction strength to hopping parameter ($U/t$) can be tuned, and the engineering process is constrained by the connectivity of $H_S$.
main_assumptions: The method assumes the existence of local fermionic unitaries that are experimentally feasible. It avoids continuous energy absorption inherent in standard Floquet driving.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the protocol, showing how local pulses modify time evolution under $H_S$ to approximate $e^{-iH_T t}$. Comparisons show convergence towards exact dynamics without heating.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the general framework using conjugation and optimization (LP). It then applies this to specific models like the Harper-Hofstadter model and the Fermi-Hubbard chain, detailing how local unitaries control hopping terms and interaction ratios.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, hardware-aware tool for simulating complex correlated electron physics by circumventing native Hamiltonian limitations, which is crucial for modeling high-Tc superconductivity.
